memory_candidates.content: When authoring a bash test that asserts two production files (e.g. two SKILL.md engines) stay in agreement, extract the literal jq filter strings from both files via stable text-anchor grep rather than hand-copying the filters into the test. Hand-copied filters only prove the test agrees with itself; anchor-based extraction (grep -A<N> on a unique surrounding comment/line, then grep -oP to pull the filter between quotes) actually catches drift if a future editor changes one file's read logic but not the other's.

This repo's test-validate-handoff.sh-style scripts under core/scripts/tests/ resolve their subject file via a candidate list checked in order; convention across the suite is deploy-tree-first when the subject is invoked identically to production runtime (e.g. skill-base.sh functions calling a hardcoded .claude/-relative path), but source-store-first when the test is meant to validate a script under ACTIVE DEVELOPMENT before a redeploy has happened -- deploy-first would silently test the stale pre-edit version during implementation.

Editing a context/ prose doc's content changes its line count, which can silently drift the corresponding index-entries.json line_count declaration and fail verify-deploy.sh's doc-lint gate on the NEXT redeploy, even though the edit itself was correct. Run `bash .claude/scripts/generate-context-line-counts.sh --write` (source-store target) after any substantive content edit to a doc tracked in index-entries.json, before redeploying, to avoid a late-discovered doc-lint failure.
